source: Verbatim tables from the 'Prakriti Parikshan' Ayurvedic Constitution Self-Assessment workbook (Govardhan School of Yoga, Yoga Teacher Training), pages 9-11. Reference content for teaching/synthesis use alongside prakriti.json — not itself a scored instrument.
display_rules: Right place, right time: none of this content belongs during the 40-item questionnaire itself (the PDF withholds it — dosha labels are hidden from the test-taker, per prakriti.json response_scale note). Each block below carries a 'show_when' field naming the exact moment it should surface. Do not show a dosha's full guide block, or a dual/Sama writeup, until that dosha or combination is the person's computed result — showing all three (or all four combinations) at once defeats the 'right dosha' half of right-place-right-time.

VAT.show_when: prakriti_results.pattern includes Vata as dominant or secondary (i.e. VAT is one of the 1-2 named doshas in the classification, not merely present at low %). Never shown for a person whose result has no Vata component.
VAT.label: Vata
VAT.principle: The principle of movement. It governs breath, circulation, nerve impulses, elimination, speech and thought.
VAT.qualities_guna: Dry (ruksha), light (laghu), cold (sheeta), rough (khara), subtle (sukshma), mobile (chala)
VAT.main_seat: Colon and pelvis; also bones, joints, skin, ears and nervous system
VAT.in_balance: Creative, quick, enthusiastic, adaptable, light on their feet, inspiring communicators
VAT.out_of_balance: Anxiety, insomnia, constipation, dryness, joint pain, scattered attention, fatigue, feeling ungrounded
VAT.increased_by: Cold, wind, dry weather; travel; irregular meals and sleep; overstimulation; fasting. Vata time: 2-6 a.m. and p.m. Life stage: later years. Season: monsoon onset and early winter
VAT.asana: Slow, grounding, warming. Standing poses, forward folds, hip openers, long holds with support. Keep flows gentle and repetitive. Long Shavasana, well covered
VAT.pranayama: Nadi Shodhana, slow Ujjayi, Bhramari. Long exhalations. Use fast techniques (Kapalabhati, Bhastrika) sparingly
VAT.meditation: Body-anchored practices: body scan, Yoga Nidra, mantra japa. A fixed time and seat every day matters more than duration
VAT.teaching_this_student: Give clear structure and predictable sequences. Offer props for stability. Watch for hypermobile joints being pushed to end range. Keep the room warm and cues calm
VAT.attribute_signature: Two of Vata's qualities show up distinctively in the mind: clarity brings quick understanding paired with quick forgetting, and can tip into a feeling of inner emptiness or loneliness when out of balance; mobility brings a mind that moves fast between many things, with moods and faith that can feel shaky rather than settled (Lad, Textbook of Ayurveda, Table 5).

PIT.show_when: prakriti_results.pattern includes Pitta as dominant or secondary. Never shown for a person whose result has no Pitta component.
PIT.label: Pitta
PIT.principle: The principle of transformation. It governs digestion, metabolism, body heat, vision, intelligence and discernment.
PIT.qualities_guna: Hot (ushna), sharp (tikshna), liquid (drava), slightly oily (snigdha), light (laghu), spreading (sara)
PIT.main_seat: Small intestine and navel region; also stomach, blood, sweat, eyes and skin
PIT.in_balance: Focused, intelligent, courageous, articulate, natural leaders, strong digestion and warmth
PIT.out_of_balance: Anger, criticism, perfectionism, acidity, inflammation, rashes, burnout, competitiveness
PIT.increased_by: Heat, sun, spicy, sour or fried food, alcohol, skipped meals, deadlines and competition. Pitta time: 10 a.m.-2 p.m. and 10 p.m.-2 a.m. Life stage: adulthood. Season: late summer and autumn (Sharad)
PIT.asana: Cooling and non-competitive. Forward folds, twists, gentle backbends, Chandra Namaskar. Practise at 70-80% of capacity. Avoid hot rooms and peak-pose chasing
PIT.pranayama: Sheetali, Sheetkari, Chandra Bhedana, Nadi Shodhana. Cooling, soft breath. Avoid excess Bhastrika, especially in summer
PIT.meditation: Heart-centred practices: Maitri (loving-kindness), gratitude, open-awareness. Surrender over achievement
PIT.teaching_this_student: Cue effortlessness and ease. Discourage comparison. Invite curiosity instead of goals. They will want the 'correct' alignment, so offer it, then teach them to soften
PIT.attribute_signature: Two of Pitta's qualities show up distinctively in the mind: sharpness brings sharp memory and quick understanding paired with irritability and low tolerance for slow, tedious work; the same spreading quality that makes a Pitta rash spread across the skin shows up psychologically as wanting one's name and reputation to spread widely (Lad, Textbook of Ayurveda, Table 6).

KAP.show_when: prakriti_results.pattern includes Kapha as dominant or secondary. Never shown for a person whose result has no Kapha component.
KAP.label: Kapha
KAP.principle: The principle of structure and cohesion. It governs stability, lubrication, immunity, strength and endurance.
KAP.qualities_guna: Heavy (guru), cold (sheeta), slow (manda), oily (snigdha), smooth (shlakshna), stable (sthira), soft (mridu), dense (sandra)
KAP.main_seat: Chest and lungs; also throat, head, stomach, joints and fatty tissue
KAP.in_balance: Calm, loving, patient, loyal, strong, steady, excellent memory, great endurance
KAP.out_of_balance: Lethargy, oversleeping, weight gain, congestion, possessiveness, resistance to change, low mood
KAP.increased_by: Cold and damp weather, heavy or sweet food, daytime sleep, inactivity. Kapha time: 6-10 a.m. and p.m. Life stage: childhood. Season: late winter and spring (Vasanta)
KAP.asana: Energising, warming and dynamic. Surya Namaskar at pace, standing poses, backbends, inversions, twists. Short holds, more repetitions. Practise early morning
KAP.pranayama: Kapalabhati, Bhastrika, Surya Bhedana, strong Ujjayi. Stimulating, heating breath
KAP.meditation: Active or eyes-open practices: Trataka, walking meditation, chanting. Keep the spine upright to prevent drowsiness
KAP.teaching_this_student: Challenge them kindly, they can do more than they think. Keep energy and pace up. Short Shavasana. Give them a reason to show up: they thrive on routine once it is set
KAP.attribute_signature: Three of Kapha's qualities show up distinctively in the mind: softness brings love, care, compassion and forgiveness; stickiness brings the same cohesive quality that gives joints their compactness into a deep, lasting attachment in love and relationships; stillness brings a preference for sitting and resting over seeking activity (Lad, Textbook of Ayurveda, Table 7).

VAT_PIT.show_when: prakriti_results.pattern is exactly the Vata-Pitta dual type (dvandvaja). Shown instead of, not in addition to, the single-dosha combination write-ups for a different pairing.
VAT_PIT.label: Vata-Pitta
VAT_PIT.description: Quick, intense and creative, but prone to burnout. Both doshas are light and mobile, so grounding is the shared need. Under stress the two can alternate rather than blend: Vata's fear one moment, Pitta's anger the next, which can look like bullying one moment and self-doubt the next. What steadies you is the quality neither dosha brings on its own: Kapha's grounded, steady quality. Balance the practice by season: cooling in summer, warming in winter.

PIT_KAP.show_when: prakriti_results.pattern is exactly the Pitta-Kapha dual type (dvandvaja).
PIT_KAP.label: Pitta-Kapha
PIT_KAP.description: Strong, stable and driven: often the constitution that does well in the world, Pitta's drive tempered by Kapha's steadiness. The real risk is that success breeds overconfidence and a smugness that deflects criticism while accepting only praise. What helps is deliberately bringing in what Vata would otherwise supply: introspection, and a bit of unpredictability, rather than more comfort.

VAT_KAP.show_when: prakriti_results.pattern is exactly the Vata-Kapha dual type (dvandvaja).
VAT_KAP.label: Vata-Kapha
VAT_KAP.description: Opposites in movement but both cold. Without Pitta's fire to mediate, the two can feel like opposite pulls, light and airy versus deep and secretive, that are hard to integrate. Warmth is the common need, in food, in practice, in life generally, and emotional hurt here tends to go deep and linger, so give it time.

SAMA.show_when: prakriti_results.pattern is Sama/Tridoshaja (all three percentages within 10 points per prakriti.json scoring_notes). Genuinely rare — pair with the re-check prompt from scoring_notes rather than presenting it as a routine result.
SAMA.label: Sama (Tridoshaja)
SAMA.description: Described as the best constitution: resilient, adaptable and balanced. Genuinely rare. A questionnaire that produces this result more often means the person answered from the middle than that they are truly Sama. Practice follows the season and the current Vikriti.

teacher_trainee_reflection_questions.show_when: Only in the yoga-teacher-training context, after the person has both a Prakriti result and a completed Vikriti check (question 4 references Vikriti directly). Not shown to a general/non-YTT user of prakriti.json.
questions: Where does my Prakriti show up most clearly in my own practice?
Which dosha type would find my teaching style hardest? What would I change for them?
Which questions did I struggle to answer, and why?
Based on my Vikriti, one change to my daily practice this month:

know_the_limits.show_when: Always alongside any Prakriti or Vikriti result — this is a standing disclaimer, not tied to a specific dosha outcome.
points: It is a self-report screen, not a diagnosis. Classical assessment (Dashavidha Pariksha) includes pulse (nadi), tongue, eyes and physical examination by a trained physician.
Current state leaks into answers. Someone anxious and sleepless this year will score more Vata than they are. Age, season and illness all shift results.

Stay within your scope. As a yoga teacher you can use Prakriti to adapt practice, pace, pranayama and meditation. Diet prescriptions, herbs and treatment of disease belong to a qualified Ayurvedic doctor (BAMS). Refer when symptoms are persistent.
Never use it to label or limit a student. 'You are Kapha, so you cannot do fast flows' is a misuse. Prakriti describes tendencies, not destiny.

standardised_tools_note.show_when: Optional footnote alongside any result, or in an About/methodology page — not tied to a specific dosha outcome.
standardised_tools_note.text: For clinical or research work, the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Ministry of Ayush, has developed and validated the CCRAS Prakriti Assessment Scale, available to trained Ayurveda professionals through the AYUR Prakriti Web Portal. The Ministry of Ayush also offers a public Prakriti questionnaire at prakriti.ayush.gov.in. This workbook is an educational tool for yoga teacher training and is independent of those scales.

classical_references.show_when: Optional footnote/appendix, same placement as standardised_tools_note — not tied to a specific dosha outcome.

constitution_note: Robert Svoboda is explicit on one point worth keeping in mind for retakes: the constitution itself doesn't change, but how accurately you can see your own doesn't stay fixed either. Someone can retake this test months later and get a more accurate answer, not because their nature shifted, but because their self-understanding did. Constitutional typing is meant to be a foundation for building self-understanding, not a label to be confined by.
vikriti_context: Ayurvedic pathology describes every imbalance as following the same six-stage path: Accumulation, Aggravation, Overflow, Location, Manifestation and Specialization (Svoboda, Ayurveda: Life, Health and Longevity, ch.6). A dosha is easiest to correct at the first stage, simply built up in its home organ with only mild symptoms - which is exactly the window this Vikriti check aims for. Only from Location onward, once a dosha has travelled and settled somewhere weakened, does a specific illness begin to take shape.
